newsitem.title: UK: Copper tumbles to five-month low as stocks jump.
newsitem.headline: Copper tumbles to five-month low as stocks jump.

text.p: LME copper slid to a five-month low on Thursday morning as further deliveries of metal pressured the market.
LME data released on Thursday morning showed stocks jumped by 13,025 tonnes after a hefty rise of 17,025 tonnes on Wednesday, bringing the total to 173,350 tonnes.

Three month prices started eroding very early, ahead of the data, as traders anticipated the inventory build, dipping to $2,226 per tonne, the lowest since February 12 and down $41 from the previous kerb close.
The market later recovered to $2,252.
Most of the activity was between $2,230, where buyers were keen, and $2,240, where a great deal of liquidation occurred, a trader said.
"Now that we've had a couple of down days, I wouldn't be surprised if copper picked up a bit today," he added.

A major part of the delivered stocks, a net 6,825 tonnes, was for the Singapore warehouse, like on Wednesday. U.S. warehouses saw deliveries of 3,175 tonnes and the remainder was split between European locations with Hamburg receiving 950 tonnes.
Far Eastern deliveries were sparked by high LME prices and slow regional demand, while most of the other stocks were sucked in by the backwardation, analysts said.
So far this week, copper stocks have risen by 34,225 tonnes, with some traders saying this is only a portion of 100,000 tonnes of incoming metal that will boost stocks through mid-August.
The cash/threes backwardation was indicated $45 narrower at $140/$150. This spread is expected to contract by around $25 each day as tight days mature and fall out of the equation.
Aluminium saw some early Far Eastern selling, chipping a few dollars off Wednesday's constructive close of $1,570, traders said. It later rose to be indicated at $1,571/74.
Analysts expect aluminium to try the upside after impressively pulling off the lows. Resistance at $1,585 could be challenged, but the $1,600 mark may be too much to ask, they added.
Zinc was little changed at $1,495, up $1, after touching the $1,500 mark again on Wednesday.
The market is overbought, with the 14-day RSI 2.5 points above the benchmark 70 level.
Any downside move should find initial support at the 10-day moving average at $1,477, followed by $1,445/42, where there is a small gap, said broker Brandeis in a commentary.
Nickel was looking soft after rolling to a six-month low on Wednesday. The market was probing the downside, last indicated at $6,666/85, versus a previous close of $6,720.
Falls to $6,600 and $6,500 were expected as weak fundamentals worry the market, analysts said. Stocks of stainless steel are high while Russian imports have boosted supply.
Tin was also shaky at $5,430, down $20 and hovering at Wednesday's 2-1/3 year low. Next support was pegged at $5,350.
Lead was up slightly at $641 and alloy was last at $1,427, versus $1,423/28.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
